Laszczow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Łaszczów, Poland

Not demolished. Łaszczów's Jewish population reached an extraordinary 93 percent of the town by 1921. In the 1770s and 1780s, the kehilla bought two brick buildings salvaged from a destroyed castle and converted them into a synagogue and beit midrash. This cemetery, established by at least the first half of the 18th century, was destroyed by the Germans during WWII and further stripped by local residents afterward. Between 1990 and 1994, at the initiative of the Jewish community of Łaszczów in Israel, the remaining portion was cleaned and fenced, and the remains of 124 victims exhumed from mass graves outside the cemetery were reburied there.
